messages.author: 9bd8300ad488fa9d
messages.subject: RMS  Value "Unit" or Scale
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering what unit or scale the value the RMS function returns is in. For example my code below..


soundrms<-rms(env(soundfile,plot=F))

1530924

I used to get RMS values from the GUI based Amadeus sound editor, where RMS was in dB. I suspect the answer to this question is quite so simple, as it might have to be "calibrated".

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 65c82d09eac308cf
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] RMS  Value "Unit" or Scale
parts:
Hello Liam,
The rms() function just computes the root-mean-square of any numeric vector. It has therefore no unit.
If you apply rms() on the envelope, which is not calibrated, you end up indeed with no calibrated data but you can still compare your rms values across different recordings, as soon as the recordings have been done in similar conditions (distance to the source, recording level etc).
HTH
Jerome

best

Hello!

I'm working on frogs advertisement calls descriptions and using seewave to plot clean calls. 

My question is:  which is the correct scale to plot in the amplitude axes in my power spectrum plot?

If anyone can give me a hint here I'll be much appreciated!

please, find attached my R script and figure,

### Script###

require(seewave)

readWave("D:/Tesis/Anfibios PN CalileguaMB/Oreobates berdemenos/Advertisement_02b (1).WAV") -> O.berdemenos

layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,4,0,0),nc = 3, byrow = T),widths=c(6,3,1), heights = c(2.5,2.5,2.5,1.5))

par(mar=c(0.5,4,1,1))

spectro(O.berdemenos, flim = c(0,4),collevels = seq(-50,0,2), ovl = 85, scale = FALSE,axisX = FALSE,font.lab = 1, grid = FALSE)

spec(O.berdemenos, fft = 512, flim = c(0,4), font.lab=1, plot = 2, norm = FALSE, scale = TRUE)

par(mar=c(0.5,1,3,2))

dBscale(collevels = seq(-50,0,2),side=4, textlab="dB", cexlab=0.65, fontlab=1)

par(mar=c(4,4,0,1))

oscillo(O.berdemenos, bty="o", cexlab=0.65,fontlab=1, from = 0, to = 1.5)

cheers,
